qs.q: An experimental animal undergoes bilateral ligation of the renal arteries. What immediate compensatory change occurs in systemic vascular resistance?
o: No significant change as renal blood flow stops
Marked decrease due to systemic fluid accumulation
Transient drop from local metabolic vasodilation
Fluctuating oscillation driven by baroreceptor resetting
qs.e: Acute bilateral renal artery ligation prevents the kidney from sensing pressure or releasing renin, while immediate vascular resistance remains stable.

qs.q: Which physiological mechanism directly contributes to an increase in systemic vascular resistance (SVR)?
o: Release of nitric oxide from vascular endothelium
Loss of arterial elasticity in older individuals
qs.e: Loss of elasticity causes vessels in older people to be stiff and rigid, preventing vasodilation and thereby increasing SVR and BP. Parasympathetic activation and nitric oxide actually decrease blood pressure through vasodilation.

qs.q: What is the classification of shock characterized by a decrease in systemic vascular resistance (SVR) and an abnormal distribution of blood flow?
o: Obstructive shock results from extracardiac pump obstruction.
Distributive shock results from decreased vascular resistance.
Hypovolemic shock results from actual fluid losses.
Cardiogenic shock results from myocardial pump failure.
qs.e: Distributive shock features a decrease in SVR with an abnormal distribution of blood flow causing functional hypovolemia. Hypovolemic shock involves decreased preload due to actual fluid losses.

qs.q: What is the primary reason systemic vascular resistance increases immediately after birth?
o: The pulmonary vascular resistance takes months to fall
The ductus arteriosus closes rapidly within 48 hours
The infant begins crying and releases prostaglandins
The low-resistance placenta is removed at birth
qs.e: Systemic resistance increases postnatally because the placenta, which was a low-resistance organ pulling blood, is removed. Lung expansion simultaneously decreases pulmonary vascular resistance.
